### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 743308b90c3a5877db980607c9cffd69ba6e5cd4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `669f28332e79d97d8e93bb09eed4ad71552f6715` — the merge of head `32ba36e004d5ab43cce19cc30e5fc4444ea5ca23` into base `743308b90c3a5877db980607c9cffd69ba6e5cd4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 669f28332e79d97d8e93bb09eed4ad71552f6715 && git checkout 669f28332e79d97d8e93bb09eed4ad71552f6715
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 743308b90c3a5877db980607c9cffd69ba6e5cd4 32ba36e004d5ab43cce19cc30e5fc4444ea5ca23 && git checkout -B drift-repro 743308b90c3a5877db980607c9cffd69ba6e5cd4 && git merge --no-ff 32ba36e004d5ab43cce19cc30e5fc4444ea5ca23

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 743308b90c3a5877db980607c9cffd69ba6e5cd4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-18T00:11Z

Head-sha: 7f6156c25f6f530db2c48eb99627aed9b55973cd
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34996, part of the ask-skill loop's first kept change set (os-dev report 6964461791).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Part of #34996`, base `main`. Six paths, +92/-12:
- `skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md` and its eval file (cases 10 and 11);
- the regenerated `ask-skill.generated.ts` and `skills-reference.mdx`;
- one `CEILINGS` row;
- a changeset releasing `@objectstack/skills` and `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch`.

`Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset changes skill text and the served page, with no export and no shape moved, so `no` is right here.

**Governed / size.** `check-governed-merges --pr 35038`: GOVERNED, Tier H, on `skills/**` ×2, 104 lines. The low-risk skills arm does not apply, because the changeset also releases `@objectstack/mcp`, as on #34977. So the route is the seat's fable L2, then the Tier H record and os-zhuang, as the request says.

**CI.** All green on this head.

**The edits, each against the text it changes:**
- **(a) The trigger.** The description now loads the skill for every question answered from the app's records, before the first data call, and adds "how much", "so far" and 「一共」. That matches the miss the round measured: a so-far question that named no metric never loaded the skill. Case 10 pins it.
- **(b) The term form.** A term is the user's noun phrase kept whole, without the verbs, time words and question words around it. It is consistent with the existing "do not translate or reword". It narrows what is sent and adds no word of the client's own. The examples, "travel budget" kept whole and 「报销金额」 not 「报销金额合计是多少」, are true to exact matching (ADR-0149 D3 rule 1).
- **(c) Ask-back.** The question is only about the user's own words, and a word with no match and no candidates goes to step 4. That is the D3 note's rule, stated where the client acts. The "no numerals" part is S1 below.
- **(d) The hidden-record-kind rule** in step 4: when no listed object or dataset is the kind asked about, say so and stop, and never answer from an object that only links to it. That is right for a permission-narrowed environment, and it closes the round's linked-object answer. Case 11 pins it.

**The cuts that pay the ratchet down.** Each removed clause keeps another home, as the `CEILINGS` comment says:
- "never treat a candidate as a match" lives on as step 1's 「A candidate is not a match.」 (line 49);
- "Compute nothing yet." lives on as the paragraph under the table: "no figure, and no tool call until the user answers".

**Ceiling.** 1491 → 1740. `ceil((6977 − 20) / 4) = 1740`, which I recomputed on this head. It sits at the measurement with no headroom and no other row moved, under ruling 6513306068 (letter B, cut the repeats first, then raise by the measured remainder).

**Evals.** I self-checked both new cases. Every `must_contain` token is in its `expected_output`, and no `must_not_contain` token is:
- case 10: `Claimed Amount`, `Expense Analysis`, `?`, none of `query_dataset`, `aggregate_records`, `total_claimed`, `1.`;
- case 11: `trip request`, and no tool name or 非指标口径.

Case 10's fixture is consistent with the executor's near rule: `claimed` is contained in "Claimed Amount", so there is one candidate.

**Measurement.** On the body's table (pre-#34997 grader), datasets went from 17/25 at iteration 0 to 25/25 at iteration 2. At iteration 5, which is this exact text, 问数 is 24/25 and datasets 25/25. The regraded rows follow once #35023 lands, as a body edit only.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1. "Without any numerals at all" contradicts the rows above it.** It also teaches around a grader artefact that #35023 has just fixed.
  - **The contradiction.** Step 2's several-measures row and candidates row both say to list each candidate's description. A business definition may well hold a number: "Deals over 10,000", "Revenue for FY2025", "Claims in the last 30 days". Under the new paragraph, a client must either drop or paraphrase that definition, which is the very text D1 says outranks the client's own reading, or break the rule.
  - **The grader artefact.** The measured failures behind (c) were `asked-back:no-figure` reading option places (「第 1 个」) and dates after a time word as figures. Under the grader's rev 2 (#35023, ACCEPTed and landing), neither is a figure any more. So the blanket ban is broader than the defect it was measured against.

  Please narrow the sentence to what the check is about. For example: "no figure of your own: no count, no total, no option number ('1.', 'option 2'); quote each description as it is written." Then re-measure under rev 2, or at least show that the narrowed text holds case 10. The ceiling moves only by the measured bytes. If the seat's L2 judges the blanket form the better trade, that ruling closes this item instead.

### Notes
- N1. Rule (d) relies on the model judging "is that kind". A user's synonym for a listed object ("deals" for `opportunity`) must not trip it. Case 11 tests only the true positive. A later eval case with a synonym that should not decline would guard the false positive. Not owed.
- N2. Case 10's `must_not_contain: "1."` is a layout token. It catches "1." but not "①" or "(1)". It is acceptable as a self-check, and #34789-style over-literal assertions are a known trade. Not owed.

Next: S1, a skill-text change that takes a ceiling re-measure and an L1-c delta read. Then the seat's fable L2 (published-skill rule change), the Tier H record and os-zhuang. The body's regraded rows after #35023 need no re-read unless the head moves.

**Delta.** One commit on top of my ACCEPTed head. It touches two paths, +6/-6: the skill's ask-back sentence and the regenerated `ask-skill.generated.ts`. Tier H is unchanged (`skills/**`).

**S1, in the skill: closed.** The sentence now reads: "State no figure of your own in it (no count, total or option number): name each option by its label in a bullet, and quote its description as written."
- The contradiction is gone. A description is quoted as written, so a definition that holds a number keeps it, as step 2's rows and D1 ask.
- The ban now covers exactly the client's own figures (a count, a total, an option number), which is what `asked-back:no-figure` checks. Dates and years are no longer banned, matching the grader's rev 2.

**Ceiling.** 6979 bytes, so `ceil((6979 − 20) / 4) = ceil(6959 / 4) = 1740`. That is still at the row, and I recomputed it on this head.

**Measurement.** Iteration 6, offline on grader rev 2 (the #35023 branch): 问数 25/25, datasets 24/25, asked-back 9/10, 0 leaks. Overall it equals iteration 5. The body names the one miss, a correct Chinese ask-back with no "？", as a grader false negative. That is plausible, but I have not checked it against the recording. If it holds, it belongs to a grader follow-up, not to this skill.

**CI.** It was running on this head when I read it (25 pending, nothing failed). This verdict holds on the condition that `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` finish green on this head.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1′. Three texts still describe the old rule. They are text only, and the changeset reaches customers.**
  - **The changeset**, which ships as `CHANGELOG.md`. The summary line says "asks back without numerals", and its third bullet says "carries no numerals at all … with no counts, dates or years". Please restate both as the new rule: no figure of its own, labels in bullets, descriptions quoted as written.
  - **Eval case 10's `expected_output`.** It says "It carries no numerals at all: no figure, no count of claims, no date or year, and no numbered option." Please align that sentence with the new rule. The assertions themselves still hold, because the expected reply has no figure.
  - **The `CEILINGS` comment.** It says "an asked-back reply carries no numerals", and its arithmetic reads 6977 bytes and `ceil(6957 / 4)`. The file is now 6979 and `ceil(6959 / 4)`. Same row, so only the comment moves.

  None of this changes the skill text or the ceiling. A push of those three files gets a short delta read.

### Notes
- N1 and N2 of my first read stand as notes, and neither is owed.

Next: S1′, then the seat's fable L2, the Tier H record and os-zhuang.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `32ba36e004d5ab43cce19cc30e5fc4444ea5ca23`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ask/evals/metric-selection-fallback.json + packages/mcp/src/ask-skill.generated.ts, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs
Security-touching: yes

PR #35038 (Part of #34996), net diff against `main` (merge-base `44430146`), six paths, +94/-12. Read: the card's body and both comments (claim 6963056752, os-dev report 6964461791), the PR body and its five comments (three L1 records, the docs-drift note, the review claim), the diff, the cited code in the head tree, and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the diff and the head tree were read with `git diff` / `git show` only.

This review is rendered at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` and covers the measured skill wording the dev authored at `TIER_DEFAULT` (the PR body's served-tier line, which names `TIER_DEFAULT`, stays as the truthful account of the authoring): every changed sentence of `SKILL.md` and both new eval cases were judged here against the code they teach, not taken from the authoring run.

Why the security line reads yes: the step 4 hunk teaches behaviour on a permission boundary. It tells the client that records of a kind it cannot list "may be hidden from you" and that it must never answer from a different object that merely links to them, i.e. not to reconstruct a withheld object through a lookup on a visible one. That is permission behaviour the path name does not show. The direction is the restrictive one (it narrows what the client answers), and it agrees with the `membersWithheld` row already on `main`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set.** No schema, no tool input or output, no executor and no door changes. No value is newly accepted or refused anywhere. Right.
- **Public surface, skill text.** `skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md` (published in `@objectstack/skills`) changes its frontmatter description (the trigger) and three body passages: the term form in step 1, the ask-back paragraph under step 2's table, a new first bullet in step 4. Two clauses leave step 2's `candidates` row. Right: each is judged in ④.
- **Public surface, served page.** `packages/mcp/src/ask-skill.generated.ts` changes the text `GET /mcp/skill` serves under "Answering a business question". Read against the generator's rule (`scripts/gen-mcp-ask-skill.mjs`: every line after the one H1, blank ends dropped, each line a single-quoted literal): the head's module holds 89 literals and the head's skill body is 89 lines, equal line for line after unescaping. The module is the regeneration, not a hand edit. Right.
- **Generated docs.** `content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx` changes one paragraph, the "Use for" sentence of the Ask entry, and it is the new description's middle sentence word for word. Consistent with the source; generated output, not reviewed further.
- **Gate row.** `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` moves one `CEILINGS` row, `skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md` 1491 to 1740. The head's file is 6979 bytes; less the 20-byte stamp line, `ceil(6959 / 4) = 1740`. Pinned at the measurement, zero headroom, no other row moved. The comment's arithmetic holds on the tree: `main`'s file is 5981 bytes, +1057 text, -61 cuts (the two removed clauses are 40 and 21 bytes), +2 for the narrowed sentence, 6979. Right.
- **Raise path.** The gate's own header (lines 155-169) recognises a raise when the diff shows deletion of restatement in the same file and the PR body quotes the standing ruling. Both hold: the diff deletes ", and never treat a candidate as a match" and " Compute nothing yet." from the `candidates` row, and the PR body quotes 「A:先削重复,余额按实测提高」 with record 6513306068, letter B. Each cut keeps another home in the same file: step 1 line 49 "A candidate is not a match." and line 64 "no figure, and no tool call until the user answers". The 10402 principle (no growth for a small feature) is not breached in my judgment: +249 buys four behaviours, each tied to a measured miss on the card, and the restatement available in the touched rows was cut first. Right.
- **Eval file.** Two cases added, ids 10 and 11, ids 1-11 distinct, the file's existing shape. For all 11 cases every `must_contain` token is a literal substring of its own `expected_output` and no `must_not_contain` token is (read off the JSON; the grader is `answer.includes`, literal and case-sensitive, `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md:765-767`). Right.
- **Check-runs on this head (56).** No run has failed. Completed with success: Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset (both), Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards (both), Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · ESLint, Lint · scoped (tooling self-tests, query-options erasure, slot lookup & corpus), Type Check · workspace, source gates and debt ledger, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate. The rest of the completed runs are path-filtered skips.
  ⛔ Still `in_progress` at my last read (2026-11-18, after 00:46Z): **Test Core 1/10 to 10/10, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates**. Test Core carries `skill-single-source-34686.test.ts`, the pin that holds the generated module equal to the skill. I read the two as equal, but a pending run is not a verdict. This record's PASS is on the reading of the tree; the seat confirms those thirteen runs green on this head before it adopts the record, and a red one voids it.
- **PR prose, not reviewed, named for the seat.** The PR title still says "numeral-free ask-back" and the body's ratchet paragraph still reads "5961 -> 6957 priced bytes, `ceil(6957 / 4)`"; the tree is 6959. The body's "id 10 (... no numerals, no figure)" is the same leftover. If the title becomes the squash subject it describes the rule L1 S1 narrowed away. A body and title edit; no head move.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/34996-ask-skill-iter-2.md` releases `@objectstack/skills` and `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch`. That is what the diff publishes: the skill's text in one package and the generated copy that ships in the other's `dist`. No export, type, schema, tool name, tool input or served route changes; the page at `GET /mcp/skill` keeps its shape and changes its words. `patch` is right for both, and `@objectstack/mcp` must be named because its built output changes. The changeset's four bullets state the head's text accurately, including the narrowed ask-back rule ("states no figure of its own (no count, total or option number) ... its description is quoted as written").

Clause-②: no — correct. Nothing a consumer compiles or parses against narrows or moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` — correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev open question 1, served tier** (authored at `TIER_DEFAULT` where `skills/**` authoring mandates `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`). Answered: option A, as the seat ruled. This record is that review; see the statement under the header. I add one limit: it covers the wording as text against code. It does not re-measure the wording.
- **Dev open question 2, grader order** (the claim says iteration 0 is rerun on the #34997 grader before any comparison, and #34997 lands first; #35023 was still open). Partly answered by the tree's history, the rest escalated to the seat as a landing condition, not a text finding. The PR body reports the head's exact text as iteration 6 on grader rev 2, so the kept text is already read on the new grader; iterations 0-5 are not. The card's rule is "keep a change only when the 5-rep round improves on the last kept one", and the only same-grader comparison for the baseline is still owed. The margin the body reports (datasets 17/25 to 24/25, asked-back 3/10 to 9/10) is far larger than a grader revision that only stops counting option places and dates as figures should move, but that is my inference and not a reading. Escalated: the regraded iteration 0 row goes into the PR body before the Tier H record, as the body's own acceptance note promises.
- **Measurements are not verified here.** The records under `/mnt/project-files/issue-34869/skill-iter/` are outside this review's inputs. The scores are the PR body's account; ④ rests on the tree. The one claim I can check against a fixed number holds: the card's target is asked-back at or above 8/10 and iteration 6 reports 9/10.
- **Dev deviation: two cuts not in the measured v2 text.** Answered: both are restatements with a surviving home (①), and the body reports them measured as iteration 5.
- **Dev out-of-scope note, the over-long line** (`SKILL.md:69`). Accepted as a deviation: a re-wrap moves no token and would change the measured bytes for nothing; the generated module carries the same line.
- **L1 S1 and S1′.** Both closed on this head, read in the tree: `SKILL.md:65-67` carries the narrowed sentence, and the changeset, eval 10's `expected_output` and the `CEILINGS` comment state the same rule. No "numerals" wording is left in any file of the diff.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5).** No query, no id materialisation and no in-app join is added: the diff is text, a generated string array, an eval file and one number. Nothing to find.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md`, each taught clause against the code on the head.**

- **(a) The trigger** (frontmatter, lines 8-13). The description is 829 characters. It widens from "a number, a ranking ..." to every question answered from the app's records, before the first data tool call, and keeps both exclusions (metadata work, application-code queries to `objectstack-query`). No other published skill claims that ground: `skills/README.md:57` and `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:186` both route the connected agent's question to this skill. It agrees with `DATASET_SELECTION_RULE` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts:1819-1827`), which already tells a client to look for a governed metric first. Holds.
- **(c) The term form** (lines 38-42). True to the matcher. A hit is equality after `normalizeDatasetTerm` and nothing else (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-term-matcher.ts:58-68`), so "trip days requested" or 「报销金额合计是多少」 cannot equal a label that "trip days" or 「报销金额」 equals. A fragment does produce answers that are not the user's: `isNear` is containment either way (`dataset-term-matcher.ts:138-145`), so "budget" alone draws every member whose name, label or synonym contains it as `candidates` (`:171-199`). The sentence adds no word of the client's own, so it stays inside "do not translate or reword". Holds.
- **(b) The ask-back paragraph** (lines 64-69). "State no figure of your own ... quote its description as written" agrees with rows 58 and 60 (list each candidate's label, its dataset's label and its description) and with the tool description, which asks for the same three things (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-tools.ts:91-95`). A description that holds a number is quoted with it, so the contradiction L1 S1 named is gone. "Ask only about matches or candidates for words the user wrote ... go to step 4" is the tool description's last branch ("No match and no candidates: fall back", `dataset-tools.ts:95-96`) and ADR-0149 D3's amendment note ("With no candidate, rule 4 is unchanged"). It also follows from the executor: a term has candidates only when it has no hit in any listed dataset (`dataset-term-matcher.ts:186-188`), and every candidate carries the `term` it was offered for, so "some other word's matches" is checkable from the answer. Holds.
- **The two cuts** (row 60). "never treat a candidate as a match" survives at line 49 and in both other carriers of the rule (`dataset-tools.ts:94-95`, `mcp-server-runtime.ts:1825`); "Compute nothing yet." survives at line 64. No rule is lost and none now reads differently. Holds.
- **(d) The declined record kind** (lines 87-90). Consistent with what the door serves: `list_objects` lists what this caller is served and hides the rest (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts:2569-2611`; the served page says so, `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts:426-427`), and `list_datasets` leaves out a dataset the caller may not query "the same answer as one that does not exist" (`packages/spec/src/ai/dataset-tools.zod.ts:219-221`). "They may be hidden from you" is hedged, and it is the same stance as row 62's `membersWithheld` wording. It does not collide with step 5 (data that records nothing): step 5 is for a missing fact, this bullet for a missing record kind, and the bullet is the stricter of the two. Holds.

**`skills/objectstack-ask/evals/metric-selection-fallback.json`, against the skill and the executor.**
